Pre-purchase inspection

Thinking of buying a Porsche? Know its condition and service needs before you commit.

What Porsche owners
ask about.

IMS bearing

M96/M97 engines: 996 and 997.1 911, 986 and 987.1 Boxster and Cayman

One of the most discussed Porsche topics. Ask about inspection and options — especially before buying one of these cars.

Coolant pipes

First-generation Cayenne V8 (955/957)

The original plastic coolant pipes under the intake can crack with age and heat.

Air-oil separator

Many water-cooled flat-six models

Smoke at start-up, high oil consumption or a rough idle can point to a failing AOS.

Bore scoring

M96/M97 engines and some Cayenne V8s

A ticking sound, rising oil consumption or a sooty tailpipe is worth a closer look.

Radiators & front cooling

911, Boxster and Cayman

Front-mounted radiators collect road debris. Cleaning and inspection help head off leaks and overheating.

PDK & transmission service

PDK and Tiptronic models

Fluid service intervals matter. Ask what’s due for your car’s age and mileage.

Good to
know.

Do I have to use the dealer to keep my Porsche warranty?

Generally, no. Under the federal Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, a manufacturer can’t void your warranty or deny coverage just because maintenance was done by an independent shop.

Follow the factory maintenance schedule and keep your records. Repairs covered by the warranty itself are still handled by the dealer.

Are you affiliated with a manufacturer?

Houston Auto Pros is an independent European automotive shop with no manufacturer affiliation.

What happens after I send a request?

A request isn’t a confirmed booking. The shop reviews it and contacts you to confirm a time and talk through what your car needs.
